In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of AAs materials based on spent FCC as an alternative binder for the construction industry.
the use of spent FCC as raw material in order to produce AAMs.
the use of spent FCC as SCM and AAM in the production of concrete and mortars, respectively, with a view to contributing to sustainable development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

AAM based on FCC is a promising alternative binder with low CO2 emission, which can be produced with a wide range of SiO2: Na2O ratios, although a minimum SiO2/ Na2O of 1.5 is required to obtain a good mechanical strength and a good workability.

the SiO2/NA2O molar ratios and the H2 O/FCC mass ratio influence the mechanical strength of alkali- activated materials based on spent FCC and that the optimum conditions to obtain a good mechanical strength are a SiO2/ Na2O molar ration of 3.5 and an H2O/ FCC mass ratio of 1.5.

the SiO2/ Na2O molar ratios of 1.0 and 2.0, as well as the H2O/ FCC mass ratio of 1.2, are the optimum conditions for the production of alkalinactivated materials based on spent FCC, in which the compressive strength of the hardened material reaches values of 40 MPa after 28 days of curing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spent FCC is a suitable material for the production of AAMS.
the use of spent FCC as a raw material for the production of AAs materials is a promising alternative to reduce the CO2 emissions associated with Portland cement production.
the mechanical strength and durability are improved with the increase of SiO2 in the spent FCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spent FCC can be used as SCM in blended cement production or as a raw material to produce AAMs, which are environmentally friendly alternatives to Portland cement.
spent FCC can be used in the production of AAsMs, and that the mechanical strength of the AAsMs can be increased by increasing the NaOH/Na2O ratio.
spent FCC can be used to obtain alkali-activated mortars with mechanical strengths higher than those obtained by the use of Portland cement (OPC).
